references.text: Shortly before this speech, crowds had gathered around Jesus, showing the growing interest from the masses ([ref:Luk 11:29|Luke 11:29]).
Jesus warned the disciples against the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees, which is their teaching. The same image of yeast as a metaphor for false teaching ([ref:Matt 16:6|Matthew 16:6]).
Jesus explains that the yeast he warns against is not literal bread, but the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees ([ref:Matt 16:11-12|Matthew 16:11-12]).
Also in Mark, Jesus warns the disciples against the yeast of the Pharisees and the yeast of Herod, representing hypocrisy and false influence ([ref:Mark 8:15|Mark 8:15]).

Jesus accuses the scribes and Pharisees of hypocrisy – they appear clean on the outside but are full of greed and impurity on the inside. This is the hypocritical yeast Jesus warns against ([ref:Matt 23:25-28|Matthew 23:25-28]).
Jesus warns the crowds and disciples about the hypocrisy of the Pharisees: they say one thing but do another ([ref:Matt 23:1-3|Matthew 23:1-3]).

Paul uses yeast as a symbol for sin and evil, urging believers to celebrate with unleavened bread of sincerity and truth – a parallel to Jesus' warning against the yeast of the Pharisees ([ref:1 Kor 5:6-8|1 Corinthians 5:6-8]).
"A little yeast leavens the whole batch" – yeast as a metaphor for how false teaching spreads through the community ([ref:Gal 5:9|Galatians 5:9]).
Jesus speaks about the hypocrisy of those who judge others without seeing their own sin – a warning against this hypocritical attitude ([ref:Luk 6:42|Luke 6:42]).
Jesus calls the Pharisees hypocrites who honor God with their lips but have hearts far from him – a direct link to the hypocrisy represented by the yeast ([ref:Matt 15:7-9|Matthew 15:7-9]).

In the immediately preceding context, Jesus rebukes the Pharisees for their hypocrisy – they clean the outside of the cup but are full of greed and wickedness inside ([ref:Luk 11:39-44|Luke 11:39-44]).
